question: Why is potassium chloride short, and what do we do?

steps.title: Our stock in three hospitals
steps.purpose: Read on-hand stock and 28-day use where each hospital keeps it.
steps.finding: 9 stock lines across 3 hospitals, 4 presentations, in units of use.

steps.title: Where our supply is made
steps.purpose: Follow each product's label to the plants it names, and place each plant in FDA's registration file.
steps.finding: 7 plant links on 4 labels; 6 placed in FDA's registration file.

steps.title: What FDA says about this shortage
steps.purpose: Read FDA's current shortage list and its history for this drug, and any listing that names one of our own package NDCs.
steps.finding: Not on FDA's current shortage list.

steps.title: Who else makes it

steps.finding: 10 labelers make it in this form.

steps.title: What FDA found at those plants
steps.purpose: Read every FDA drug inspection, warning letter, import alert and recall for these plants.
steps.finding: 82 inspections (11 OAI at our plants), 6 compliance actions, 1 import-alert listings, 1 recalls.

steps.title: What FDA wrote at the OAI inspections
steps.purpose: Read the Form 483 observations recorded at those inspections.

steps.title: What our P&T committee already approved
steps.purpose: Read Corvale General's approved interchanges for these items.

steps.title: Which links can't be trusted
steps.purpose: Run the semantic layer's key rules (NDC and unit of use) over each hospital's stock, and name the rows they reject.
steps.finding: 11 stock rows across the system fail the NDC rule; 0 of them are this drug. Every row is in a shared unit of use.

steps.title: What we decided last time
steps.purpose: Recall past decisions on this drug from H-MEM, with who approved them.
steps.finding: No past decisions on this drug.

explanation.headline: Potassium chloride is not on FDA's current shortage list; the earlier shortage posted 2021-11-02 is resolved

sentences.text: FDA's records show potassium chloride is not on the current shortage list as of 2026-10-21; the earlier shortage first posted 2021-11-02 has been resolved.

FDA inspected multiple registered plants for this drug, including Baxter Healthcare Corporation (FEI 1416980) with an OAI classification on 2026-04-02 and a Warning Letter on 2026-09-29, Baxter (FEI 2649614) with VAI classifications in 2018 and 2023, Baxter (FEI 2618677) with multiple OAI and VAI inspections from 2010 through 2024, APL HEALTHCARE LIMITED (FEI 3011895410) with VAI inspections in 2020 and 2025, Hospira, Inc. (FEI 1021343) with OAI and VAI inspections from 2010 through 2019 and a recent NAI in 2025, and Pfizer Healthcare India Private Limited (FEI 3008316085) with an OAI in 2019 and a Warning Letter in 2020.
Corvale East holds 35 bags of the 29.8 g/1000 mL 50 mL presentation at 13 per day, giving 2.7 days on hand, while Corvale General holds 215 bags at 13.1 per day, giving 16.4 days on hand.

The rule-based best option is to transfer 31 bags of the 29.8 g/1000 mL 50 mL presentation from Corvale General to Corvale East, which would leave Corvale General with 14 days and bring Corvale East to 5 days.

Additional presentations include 14.9 g/100 mL 250 mL at Corvale East (8.9 days), Corvale General (9.7 days), and Corvale Lakeside (19.2 days), and 149 mg/mL 20 mL vials at Corvale General (16.3 days).
